title: The Age of Exploration
key_facts: European maritime powers explored and mapped coastlines and sea routes across the globe
Opened persistent transoceanic connections linking Afro‑Eurasia and the Americas
Initiated the Columbian Exchange of goods, peoples, plants, animals, and diseases
causes: Advances in navigation, shipbuilding (caravel), and cartography
Economic motives to access spices, gold, and direct trade routes
Religious and political competition among European states
outcome: Establishment of European colonies and global trade empires
Profound demographic and ecological changes via the Columbian Exchange
Foundations for the early modern world economy

figures.name: Vasco da Gama
figures.role: First sea route from Europe to India

impacts: Integration of world regions through trade, conquest, and cultural exchange
Rise of Atlantic economies and shift of power centers
Spread of languages, religions, and technologies—alongside exploitation and slavery
